questions.q: What value does an uninitialized Apex variable hold by default?
options: 0 for numbers, false for Booleans
An empty string
null, regardless of its declared type
It won't compile until a value is assigned
questions.explain: All Apex variables, whether class member variables or method variables, are initialized to null until you assign them a value.

questions.q: Which data type does Salesforce automatically assign to currency fields?
options: Double
Decimal
Integer
String
questions.explain: Decimal is an arbitrary precision number, and currency fields are automatically assigned the type Decimal.

questions.q: What happens if you assign a valid 15-character record identifier to an Id variable?
options: Apex throws a compile error immediately
Apex truncates it to 12 characters
Apex converts it to its 18-character representation
Apex stores it unchanged as 15 characters
questions.explain: If you set an Id to a 15-character value, Apex converts the value to its 18-character representation automatically.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes Date from Datetime?
options: Date and Datetime are exactly the same type with different names
Date holds only a time of day; Datetime holds only a calendar day
Date indicates a particular day with no time information; Datetime indicates a day and a time
Datetime can only be used in triggers, not in regular classes
questions.explain: A Date value indicates a particular day and contains no information about time, while a Datetime value indicates both a day and a time, like a timestamp.

questions.q: How should you create a Date or Datetime value in Apex?
options: Always using a system static method such as Date.today() or Datetime.now()
By casting a String literal directly
By declaring it with the 'new' keyword and no arguments
Date and Datetime values can't be created, only read from fields
questions.explain: Salesforce's guidance is to always create Date and Datetime values with a system static method, such as Date.today() or Datetime.now().
